row.consequences_md: Small installers and one runtime. Three WebView engines and Linux WebKitGTK packaging need testing. The UI is TS; no Node runtime ships.
row.context_md: Need a cross-platform desktop host with an embedded Discord bot, SQLite, and local files. Owner prefers Rust.
row.decision_md: Use Tauri 2.12, Rust for all core logic, React 19 + TypeScript for the UI. Do not use Electron.
row.title: Tauri 2 + Rust backend + React/TS UI

row.consequences_md: About 1-2 days of command plumbing. Plain-data events make fixtures easy. No macro framework.
row.context_md: Need guild commands, buttons, DM attachments and history, rate limits, and current API models. Need a stable crate.
row.decision_md: Use Twilight 0.18 with a thin adapter and pure domain handlers.
row.title: Twilight 0.18 for Discord

row.consequences_md: Claim-first protects the seen ledger. DM backfill is possible. Blocked DMs need a private-thread fallback. No prefix commands.
row.context_md: Interaction tokens expire in 15 minutes. Ephemeral attachments are not durable. DMs with the app are exempt from MESSAGE_CONTENT.
row.decision_md: Send offers by DM with buttons. Send the file only after Claim. Accept submissions by DM attachment. Use GUILDS and DIRECT_MESSAGES intents only.
row.title: DM-first, claim-first delivery without privileged intents

row.consequences_md: Every scheduler and override validates against it. Never relax it to rescue a slot. Retire or hold instead.
row.context_md: The core promise is that nobody works on a track twice.
row.decision_md: Record (track, participant) on claim/receipt, submit, and claim-then-skip. Do not record a pre-claim skip or expired offer. Exclude the owner separately. Never reset during the event.
row.title: Append-only seen ledger

row.consequences_md: Commit-reveal is possible. Groups layer on the same primitive. Infeasible rounds return a conflict list.
row.context_md: Need fair no-repeat schedules without a predictable cyclic pattern.
row.decision_md: Build row by row with a seeded perfect matching. Exclude the owner. Validate no repeats. Default N-1 rounds with an overcrowding warning above 12 participants.
row.title: Classic scheduling uses a randomized partial Latin rectangle

row.consequences_md: Simpler async state and less leak surface. Better reach and fewer repeat pairs. Optional content tags can come later.
row.context_md: The async simulation compared global queue, soft migration, barriers, generational queues, group-aware pools, and a social-diversity objective.
row.decision_md: Use one global queue with a social-diversity objective. Do not use participant groups, migration, barriers, or reserved queues. Classic mode keeps groups.
row.title: Async mode uses no formal groups

row.consequences_md: Faster events, fewer expired offers, lower p95 wait. Edit completeness is not promised. Full exposure takes months at large N.
row.context_md: The async simulation measured claim expiry, release timing, and completeness.
row.decision_md: Default claim window 24h with a 12h reminder. One daily release window with two dispatch waves. Completeness means exposure. Default length N-1 for 12 or fewer participants; 6-8 rounds above 12. Host can choose full exposure.
row.title: 24h claim window, two daily waves, exposure completeness

row.consequences_md: Events finish without chasing people. Some pairs remain unexposed and appear in the gap report. Credits are preserved.
row.context_md: Exposure completeness can loop forever if a participant never claims.
row.decision_md: Offer only to Ready participants. After an expiry, never offer the same track to the same person again. Apply a host-configured strike/cooldown policy. Report exposure gaps. A claimed deadline miss counts as seen.
row.title: Async anti-loop protection

row.consequences_md: Free and simple distribution. SmartScreen warns on Windows. Users download installers manually.
row.context_md: Need a simple distribution path for a public open-source desktop app. macOS signing is not funded.
row.decision_md: Build Windows NSIS and Linux .deb/AppImage in GitHub Actions. Publish GitHub Releases with SHA256SUMS and attestations. Windows is unsigned. No macOS in v1. No auto-update in v1.
row.title: GitHub Releases, Windows + Linux, unsigned, no updater

row.consequences_md: Shorter, less ambiguous specs. Writers use the glossary. Automated linting can come later.
row.context_md: Many conditional rules make ambiguous prose expensive.
row.decision_md: Use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English for PRD requirements, Gherkin, event settings, test plans, runbooks, CLI instructions, and error messages. Keep playful copy for user-facing text.
row.title: ASD-STE100 for specifications

row.consequences_md: Durable work memory without scaffold ceremony. Specs stay readable. The tracker remains the evidence source.
row.context_md: The project-scaffold has useful issues, decisions, evidence, and a ledger, but heavy PRD gates.
row.decision_md: Use the SQLite tracker for issues, decisions, evidence, sessions, and the append-only ledger. Keep the PRD, event settings, and Gherkin hand-written and editable. Use research-first TDD with worktrees. One plan review, no sign-off gate.
row.title: Lean tracker with hand-written specs
